description: Committee recommends $1.2 million for Material Recovery Center slope repair.
Funds will transfer from Waste Processing Capital Reserve.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor questioned warranty claim and impact on future projects.
Warranty claim responsibility for slope failure remains unestablished.
Warranty claim for slope failure may involve legal proceedings.
Degradation of slope and pond liner could result in significant environmental impact.

description: Committee recommends 2028/2029 budget options for monitored washrooms.
Expand monitoring to four riverbank locations.
Aims to reduce vandalism and increase washroom availability.

chips.text: Recommended
Annual operating costs estimated at $276,000 per location.
Committee directed administration to bring 2027 budget options for Shakespeare on the Saskatchewan.
Users of Shakespeare on the Saskatchewan, River Landing, Festival Site, Victoria Park Boathouse.
Administration is developing a broader public washroom strategy for 2027.

description: Recommends $3.04 million ICIP funding for landfill gas collection.
Recommends $84,000 ICIP funding for methane emission regulations.
City will not add a third landfill gas power generator.

chips.text: Recommended
Increases Landfill Optimization project by $3,039,900, and Power Supply project by $84,000.
Trevor Bell explained a third power generator is not economically feasible.
Landfill gas system destroyed 85,000 tons of CO2 equivalent in 2025.

description: Committee recommends funding fire fleet facility with $95,500.
Roadways Fleet will rent 106 Tubby Crescent from Fire.
Future lease revenue will also fund the facility.

chips.text: Recommended
Roadways Fleet received $300,000 in 2026 for heated vehicle storage.
Councillor questioned need for two vehicle storage facilities.
Affects Roadways Fleet and Support, and Saskatoon Fire Department.

description: Details city actions to remove systemic barriers for Indigenous peoples.
Outlines efforts in recruitment, engagement, and board participation.
Includes developing a reconciliation action plan and recruitment strategy.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Keller concerned about lack of clear path for future progress reports.
Indigenous peoples are affected by systemic barriers in city processes.
City is developing a smudging policy for employees.
Councillor Davis asked how reconciliation plans are embedded in all projects and budgeting.
Indigenous Technical Advisory Group (ITAG) provided feedback on systemic barriers.
Indigenous recruitment strategy expected to launch in 2027.
